title: DELETED TEXT CAN BE RECOVERED FROM NOTES!!
body:
First of all, I just wrote a long review with detailed info on this, but I jumped to another screen and when I came back, what I had written was gone!  So frustrating!  This is an Apple app ~ unfinished reviews should be able to be temp saved!

Anyway, people need to know the following info about how to recover text deleted in error!  After happening to me one too many times, I searched the internet for a solution but couldn’t find one.  Seems many others couldn’t, as well.  I even saw responses from support personnel stating that there wasn’t a resolution ~ including Apple!  I also noticed complaints about this issue in some of the reviews here.  The problem users are having is with text disappearing, or being deleted by accident, within Notes.  Not sure how it’s happening ~ seems to be when text is selected (to copy and paste, for example) and then it’s gone before it can be pasted!  I think (at least in my case), I accidentally double-tap instead of single tap (due to jerky-finger!), which the app seems to recognize as delete.  I have lost a lot of text (a day of lists), which is very frustrating.   This seemed to start happening after the recent addition of the “Note” feature within Notes (swiping up from right-hand corner).  I don’t use it (don’t really see the need/use for it?) and oftentimes I accidentally bring it up, which is annoying because it then needs to be deleted.  Developers ~ is this feature really necessary ~ especially within notes?!

So, after text was accidentally deleted again recently, I decided to try the Markup button (pencil tip icon).  I selected the back arrow option, and it WORKED ~ all the text came back!  The arrow can be pressed as many times as needed (just like in other apps) to recover the most recently lost “groups” of typed text (words, sentences, paragraphs, etc).  I think selecting “Done” while typing is what separates text.

This solution is almost too easy for people to not be aware of ~ it needs to be documented and communicated (if it’s not).  I don’t think it is, because none of the reviews with complaints about this issue were responded to by the Apple Support Team.   I will send them a message, as well.

One more side note, it seems the other features of the Markup button can also be used within notes, but not very well or efficiently.  For example, colored text can be added (which many people have requested in reviews) via the “Text” box option in Markup, but it will be SEPARATE from the other text.  So, certain words can’t be a different color, unless you want them separated by the invisible Text box (or, you can add a shape (rectangle, square, etc.) around the text.  It’s just not worth it for the Notes app, as far as I can tell.  Apple just needs to add a simple feature to enable colored text!  Thanks!

title: All of My Notes in the “Notes” App, POOF! GONE!
body:
Yesterday, Wednesday, October 18, 2023, I went to open my “Notes” app on my iphone, but the app was gone. I went to app store, got the app back, however, it was not the same version, because it did not have any of the options that my current version had, like redo and undo, re-size fonts, bold, italicize, or underline, option to add photos, etc. It was a very old version. I have spent hours since this happened, trying to find my notes, and nothing. They have just vanished. According to my online search, many people have experienced this same issue with iphone, and specifically, a large number of people since July 2023. Anything suggested online for me to try in order to recover my notes, I tried, but nothing. I did not back them up to icloud, which I regret, but apparently, they were not being backed up on my iphone or by any other application, which I was NOT aware of, so, 

HOW DID THIS HAPPEN?

WHERE DID MY NOTES GO? 

IS THERE A WAY I CAN RECOVER MY NOTES SINCE THEY WERE NOT SAVED TO ICLOUD OR BACKED UP ANYWHERE ON MY PHONE?

From now on, every note in the “note” app is saved to icloud and backed up, but, it might be best that I search for another app, a more reliable app.  I really need my notes recovered. These notes were very important to me, and some were very personal. Two plus years, and countless hours of hard work, on notes that contained a variety of information, poetry and other forms of writing, and so much more. 

I hope Apple can fix this issue, and also provide a solution that will allow myself and others to be able to recover their notes, because there are other reviewers of this app that share my painful experience. Like me, these reviewers relied 100% on this app to provide a much needed outlet to express themselves, and/or to log other important information, personal and non-personal in nature, and for many other reasons. Until they can fix this issue, I would recommend that you DO NOT use this app, because it is not reliable.

title: Wonderful UI, Horrible Safety and Compatibility
body:
Apple crushes all other note apps here in usability - trust me I have tried them all and am a prolific note taker (from daily journals to recipes to grocery lists to research data). The user experience creating and viewing notes is unmatched - and sharing notes is wonderfully easy.

But that's where it ends for me. Apple has not created any meaningful version history for regular notes - meaning a single keystroke accident can wipe data or even full notes. If you're lucky - you'll just have deleted a full note and that can be recovered within 30 days "if" you notice it. But what if you just deleted the "contents" of the note? Well, you're screwed. Oh, you say "just backup regularly"? NOPE. Apple doesnt provide a way to bulk export your notes (like every single other note app) - you can only export to pdf one at a time. So backups of your collection are not feasible.

And while Apple Notes in web browser "works", it has a very different feature set. So you can't really collaborate with someone who doesn't have a physical Apple device (to use the native app).

Sounds great right? You trade a wonderful UI for being locked into the app with no version history, no export options, and no full web browser support. "You can check in any time you like.... but you can NEVER LEAVE!" - Hotel California, The Eagles.

I wanted to use this app so bad and am annoyed at apple for what is either 1) a massive design oversight or 2) An intentional app ecosystem lock-in. Either way it's bad. I've found a mix of Todoist and DayOne to be best. DayOne will bring shared journals some time this year and then other than the UI - DayOne will be better. For now, no amount of Apple's wonderful usability is worth losing notes or never being able to get your notes out of the app

title: iPhone “Notes”
body:
All these years, I used to write down important memos on scrap paper and index cards.

Problem with them, is they will never be available when you need them. 

Now we can just open “Notes” on the iPhone.

The memos and notes and reminders are now ALWAYS available, never again a ‘misplaced’ or lost note!

And they can be edited and updated without having to search for a scrap paper or pen or pencil (All of us have a dozen pens, but you can never find a pen when you need it).

They also stay confidential in your phone, and not ‘discovered’ by anyone you don’t want to see your scrap notes.

Overall, a nice and useful feature.

title: Searching tools
body: I save a lot of notes, and some of them are quite lengthy in terms of the number of words. I often have to search for something within all my notes. If you want to search for a certain word, the only thing Notes will provide is one location in one note. After that you’re on your own doing a visual search.  I might have a note that has hundreds of words. The search system built into notes would only find the first instance of the word I’m looking for. That’s often not very helpful. If the first instance of that word in one note isn’t the exact one I’m looking for then Ive still got a searching problem. I would have to copy the whole note and paste it into Microsoft Word which does offer a much better ability to search for a particular word.  However, I would have to copy the entire text of every note that contains the word I’m searching for into word just to do this type of search.

title: Almost There… A Few Things
body: Love notes. I used to keep notes in separate text files in my Documents Folder, all under categorized folders (‘Legal’, ‘Manuals -> Mac -> iOS’ etc. etc). Then I went to Evernote, and it was much better of course - being able to search, add photos to a note, colorized text, etc., which is where Notes needs work. I work in a mixed Windows/Mac/iOS environment. I sometimes want to simply paste a picture into a note. NOT EAST TO DO IN NOTES. If the photo is on my Windows system, I have to first copy it to ny iCloud Drive, then on my iPhone, ‘Save’ the photo from the Drive into my Photos app. Only then can I import the photo into a note. Also, if I want to add color for text, I have to get off my Windows machine, and do it from my Mac. Why not make these features global? I know Apple would like me to own & work only from Apple products, but in the real world for a lot of people, this is not our reality. Apple, please make all features available globally.

title: Lost notes synced with gmail / lots of formatting bugs
body:
I use notes daily. I have almost 12,000 of them. 

I’m kind of committed so I’m staying here. But on my mac, a few months ago an update happened and I’m no longer able to press cmd + B for bold font (underline and italic shortcuts still work). Also, on phone and mac, sometimes I’ll write a number or date like “1949” and put a period after it. And it will bizarrely think that I’m trying to make a list. And will screw up the number, indent and reformat everything, and start a list that is very hard to get rid of. 

And just in general it too often goes into list or numbering mode and is VERY hard to get out of once it starts. And your formatting is likely screwed up for the whole rest of the note so I just start a new note. 

What brings me to writing this poor review now (honestly, the phone prompted me to leave a review), but is because I recently got a new phone and thus had to reauthorize my password to get my Mail app working with my gmail account. (Notes had been working just fine without reentering my password). But when i went to enter my gmail password again, the mail now works but many of my notes were lost. And what is most disorienting and confusing and frustrating and depressing is that it seems to have erratically affected them. Some notes are now incomplete or at earlier stages of completion, other notes are entirely missing, and without even much of a pattern. Looking at all my notes on one given day, some notes will be entirely missing, some notes will be in earlier versions, and some will be 100% there. Very frustrating. Did some googling and I guess this exact thing has happened to several other people. You re-enter your password and you lose your notes. Thankfully I didn’t lose them all, other people lost them all. So now I’m paying to get an icloud subscription in the hope that Icloud will be a bit more secure than Gmail. But who knows. Oh also, using gmail in general with the notes app is a nightmare on your gmail. It wrecks your gmail search function. It saves a copy in your gmail of like EVERY single version of a note. So if my note is “it’s a good day”

It’ll save one note for “it” another for “it’s” another for “it’s a” another for “it’s a good” 

Etc. And if a note is several thousand words long, there are severla thousand versions of one note saved in my gmail. Given that i have almost 12,000 notes. I probably have several hundred thousand versions of notes in gmail. So if i try to search for really ANYTHING in gmail, it comes with one of my many many many notes, so I have to make sure to use very specific filters as my search function is basically useless given the overpopulation of notes in general search. 

Thanks,
Austin

title: Probably nowhere near the best but it works
body:
As an aspiring author who has over 200 notes with a few of them withholding an impressive amount of words that shouldn't be the length of a single chapter in a first novel that also so happens to be fiction, this app is the backbone to the wonderous worlds I'm creating. I've managed to take the flame of an idea and light traditional writing of fire so the I can take that flame and condense it into digital notes for a beautiful world to be born. For example, I will state my practice writing in the spaces below for your entertainment. By the way I know the name is weird.

Gleam stepped into the clearing, her eyes widening as she saw what was in it. There, on the threshold of where Gleam’s forward path through life began to falter, was a fallen tree, barren of leaves with a trunk so pale it looked as if it had been adorned by the moon’s mournful cloak. And there, on that tree, was her grandma. She was lying so still, her hands being held so tightly by Gleam’s mother, father, and innocent little sister as they watched her face go pale, and her eyes begin to glaze over in finality. Tears were streaming down her mother’s cheeks, her eyelids red, and the darkness of losing her mother shadowing her irises. Gleam’s father was shuddering with a cold only a husband could feel, his arm wrapped around his wife’s shoulders in an attempt to comfort her, but all it really provided was something for Mom’s tears to fall on.

And then there was her sister. 

her eyes watched everything confused, just beginning to grasp, at last, what was going on. There was no energy left in Gleam to drag her away from this horrible, sickly place, though, and all she could do was stand frozen like a statue, unable to move or do anything to prevent the sadness, for it had already come down on them anyways. She could do nothing.

Vicious screaming inside Gleam’s mind was realizing at last that everything was wrong.

“Grandma---” she tried to scream, to call out to her for that small hope that she would sit up and give Gleam a warm, familiar smile, and tell her not to worry, and that she will be back before Gleam knew it-- but all that came out was a pitiful whisper, and grandma didn't get up-- couldn't get up. She would never again.

You knew this would happen, you've had all the time in the world to prepare for it. Her mind tried to reason, but it didn't make anything better. No matter what her mind said, it would always sting more than anything in the world. And she didn't have time, nothing had time, or everything had time. she didn't even know anymore. all she knew was the thumping of her heart as gunshots threatened her life, and the burning hot tears that sliced her cheeks and stuffed their sadness through the wound and into her mouth until she had no choice but to suffocate in it.

Tears were beginning to well from her eyes, but she swallowed them down. She had to stay strong. For her sister. 

“I wish we had more time.” Gleam’s mother said, her voice almost a whisper. She traced the lines of her mother’s smile, as if expecting her to follow them and bubble out her signature sweet laugh. It never came.

Her sister had gotten up from playing in the dirt and watching, realizing what was happening. 

“Grandma?” she copied Gleam, louder, though, and more urgent. 

She walked hesitantly towards Grandma-- but Gleam lifted her off of her feet and flung her back before she could get there.

“Let her come.” Gleam’s mother ordered, all of her life and spirit drained from her voice. “Let her say goodbye.”

And so Gleam let her sister down, grabbing her hand tightly, and beckoning her towards Grandma’s form. 

In summary, notes is all you need.

title: Notes and Art
body: I have been enjoying working with Notes so much more since so many improvements have been made in the past few years. In particular, I have been using the sketch feature for either writing by hand, or more recently, to work on sketches for my art. I enjoy working in several mediums, but it’s gotten so easy to just pick up my Apple Pencil and put a sketch on my handwritten notes. In fact, I have started using Notes for some of my artwork. I like the way colors are expressed on Notes better than my usual go to art app. The colors are easy to mix and I can find any color that I want. The only improvement would be is if you made an area where I could store special colors that I use frequently while working on a piece. The tools are fun and useful to work with and help make it easier for me to execute certain parts of my work. I really enjoy that I can also make us of typing a poem or words into my paintings if I want in a large variety of fonts and sizes. However, having said all that, I have encountered a serious problem that has been occurring repeatedly over the past 2-3 days. While I’m in sketch mode, Notes has been crashing without saving my work. Sometimes the lost work is significant. I can lose hours of work this way. I have tried closing everything and rebooting to no effect. It still happens. And there’s one other thing that might mean nothing. While I work, I almost always listen to music, either on headphones or on a speaker. I have noticed that when using the sketch mode and while listening to music at the same time, my iPad becomes very hot to the touch. I have checked settings to see if I should stop working, but according to the Apple article I read about it, as long as the message about overheating doesn’t come on, it should be fine. Since I don’t trust everything I read, I usually stop to give the iPad a cooling off period. But I noticed that my iPad doesn’t overheat when I use my usual art app, Pencil while listening to music. It will warm up, but it won’t get very hot as it does with Notes. I hope you can find the problem. Until then, I’ll be using just my art app.

title: Good, but missing key features.
body:
The app is generally great but lacks key features that force users to rely on third-party apps for more serious work. These missing features include:
1) The notes app cuts and splits handwritten notes, and it lacks visible page indicators and/or automatic adjustments for printing and exporting. Adding visible indicators like a small marker and a full-page setup option would be beneficial. This would allow users to skip lines when taking handwritten notes and avoid writing on the page break unknowingly. Having the option to switch to a full-page setup, like writing on letters or A4-sized notes with multiple pages instead of a continuous roll, would be helpful as well.
2) Although the new feature that opens notes straight to the Apple Pages app is appreciated, it converts handwritten notes to an image instead of text, which is not useful. This forces users to convert their handwritten notes to text manually.
3) Users are unable to zoom in for more precise details or change the type of tool used for handwriting or drawing, similar to other apps.
4) Users are unable to highlight text or draw or scribble on top of it using the Apple Pencil.
5) The app still lacks the ability to change the color of text.

title: Splendid! But just a couple of ideas...
body:
I love this app with a passion. It is probably the best note-taking app I have ever gotten. All the other note-taking apps are just so confusing, but this one is amazingly easy to use. 

However, I have a couple of ideas for what you can add in the future...

1) First of all, I think that we should be able to change the format on the same line. For example, let's say I want some words to be subheading, and some other words on the same line to be just normal. It won't let you do that. Only one line can be the same format. That is kind of annoying it, to be honest. Maybe you could change that? Just an idea!

2) And second, I think that we should be able to draw on the same place as the text. For example, let's say I am typing a paragraph about Africa, and I want to draw something in the background, like the sun, or an animal, but it won't let me do that. It will only let me draw where text isn't, which is below it, which is annoying. To me, that is. Again, this is just an idea. 

Thank you for reading, and I hope you have a good day!

title: Helpful, but inconsistent.
body:
Notes, it basically goes by two editions, there’s the iPhone/iPad, and the Laptop/iMac.
Each one has something different going on, to the point where it feels like Apple should have a lil’ “version” indication next to the app’s name, because here’s the thing:
The iPhone/iPad edition was cleaned up, a lot. You’ve got lil’ buttons that pull up menus, basic fonts such as Italic, Bold, Underline, etc.
Over the past few years, they’ve added a feature where you can sketch on the paper, I’m someone who doodles a lot so I got all giddy, because hey I can make myself visuals of my grocery list, and that, just makes it fun. But the thing about Notes is that it can be difficult to use on an iPhone, there are so many little buttons, so many features, to the point I feel like Apple needs to offer a literal Tutorial option somewhere. Just to show all the special tap-combos, swipes and such; and I know they’ve got a website or the Tips App for this, but if you’re like me, by the time you get back into the app, you won’t remember what it was you were going to write down, because when you get into the Tips App, or Apple’s Website, you might just get drawn in by all the colorful videos or you just get lost trying to find information on the one thing. Now, have I, by now, looked at all these sources to learn about Notes? Yes I have, and let me tell you something.. I had no idea you could shake your iPhone- to pull up the Undo option. Where was that when I deleted half of a script by accident? A back-button is something I feel should be in the “+” button slab, it’s just something that we use too frequently that’s too hidden from the user’s knowledge. And you know, if I’m just stupid, that’s fine, I’m just trying to look out for others in my position.
How I feel about the iPhone/iPad edition of Notes is mixed due to these various issues, but now we’ve got ourselves the Laptop/iMac edition:
I’m someone who works at the computer a lot, Pages is an App I’ve got but hesitate to use because of how advanced it is, which is fine, the couple times I’ve used it it’s gotten the job done. I’m more of a Notes guy, it’s a touch more simple, and I can easily access my ideas and thoughts quickly across devices when I’m on the go- or chilling on the couch three feet away from the iMac. Here’s what I found strange and hence the title of the review “Helpful, but inconsistent”.
You can color text, change the point-size of selected text, and even access fonts? Actual fonts, I could make my comic script have a Whatahburger font, and that is fantastic. But why is that a thing here but not there? The iPhone/iPad edition does not have a feature like that. I like to make my things look fancy, having a color wheel is the way to go, but it’s not there.

I’ll give Notes a 5 when Apple decides to explain their features more clearly, and when they keep these two editions balanced, equal, and consistent.

—I.F

title: Great for work
body:

A few feature requests:

-Integrate lists in notes with the reminders app. I love to have a daily note with a to-do list at the top, but the reminder app is such a better task app compared to the checklist text option in notes. Wish I could embed a reminders list into my daily note.

-Calendar view option. I love the notes sorted by date, but for work, I sometimes need to find a note I wrote on a specific date months or years ago. Would be great to find it in a calendar view.

-Templates. I have a janky hack for note templates by having a few pinned notes that I copy/paste — i.e. meeting notes, daily notes, 1:1s, etc. Would be great to hold down the new note button and be able to choose from a few templates.

title: Hands down the best service Apple offers.
body:
And that’s saying a lot, considering what Apple Notes is up against: all the other magical Apple apps, software features, and products that each occupy a league of their own in their respective classes. 

I use Apple Notes daily as a university student. It is the only note-taking platform I use; I don’t carry around physical notebooks or download other note-taking apps. Some features of Apple Notes make it invaluable: the simple interface, iCloud integration, the scanning function, being able to copy/paste screenshots into my notes, tags and smart folders, the monospaced format (useful for taking notes for computer science), the ability to lock notes, etc. No matter what device I’m on (I use a MacBook, iPhone, and iPad), all my notes are in sync and can be accessed anywhere. 

It’s not perfect, though. Handwritten notes become extremely laggy once you start writing a lot—this is frustrating when you’re working through math homework and strokes just start randomly disappearing. This is the case regardless of if you’re using an older iPad or newer Apple silicon iPads. 

I’m eager to see what the Apple Notes team has in mind for the future of this app. It’s one of those magical products that’s profoundly simple but infinitely powerful.
author: Apple Notes Fan

title: My most-used app
body:
To say I love and depend upon this app would be an understatement. By now I've accrued years' worth of valuable notes, thoughts, writings, journal entries...the ease of use and the simplicity of this app is its greatest appeal. 

iPhone's introduction of spoken–word type a few years ago only increased my dependence, too. Voice typing can be faster than normal or swipe typing, but it also saves your hands from pain and fatigue. And so, it is on this amazing feature my complaint hangs. 

A huge amount of my time is now wasted in deleting superfluous commas and other punctuation this feature automatically adds to my notes.  This so called "smart programming" is probably an attempt to save time, but I cannot stress enough how terrible and frustrating and poorly it works. Leave the punctuation to me, please! As a writer, this is utterly crucial. Apple, please return voice typing back to its original simplicity…the only updates I want are an increased accuracy of my enunciation (which, happily, I've noticed has already improved since the feature was introduced).

title: A product worthy of Microsoft
body:
Anyway I upgraded my iPhone, which of course came with updated software. Many thanks for most of the numerous upgrades. 

However, the Notes app, which I use for, well, all sorts of notes in place of napkins and envelopes, has a new “feature” which:

1. Can’t be turned off
2. Can’t be changed, and;
3. Works terribly anyway 

Of course, that is the whole automatic formatting function that was added.

1. How did that feature even get proposed in the first place?
2. How did it get through all the software reviews?
3. How? Why?

Please, please, please add a prominent control to turn it off. Keep it if you like, but at the very least add some controls for formatting rules. 

By the way, this review would have been impossible to write in Notes, because it would have kept formatting things. 

For the project manager and your Agile board:

The use-case is that I collect assorted notes and comments that may include makeshift lists. The Notes app is a convenient place to do it before sending it along via email or another app. Don’t try to turn Notes into a word processor, a web browser, or some other application.

title: Perfect but for file type
body:
I’ve used Apple notes forever and every day. It’s done everything I’ve asked of it even though it has no bells and whistles, no fancy notebooks or I don’t even know what else it might be missing. It’s been great. A couple years ago I was curious about other notes apps so I took stock of how I use this and any drawbacks I’ve noticed. I haven’t had problems and I couldn’t find anything that seemed better. 

********†*******†*******†****†****†***†***†***†*†****†*†

 Now it’s crashing. I’m stuck deciding what to use instead because I can’t find another app to import my 4000+ notes and will store securely in the cloud. App descriptions have always seemed obtuse and no more so than when I really need something. Dealing with my notes all I can do is rush in, grab what I need and rush out before it crashes. It’s a quandary every time I need to save some thing. Apparently the file type is one that doesn’t work with any other and of course I’ve spoken with various Geniuses.

It’s been 18 months or more since Notes began crashing. I haven’t lost data but I haven’t been able to take advantage of anything new because it chronically crashes. I’m frustrated because all I want are simple folders to fill with files- at it’s most basic form I want something to make outlines. I know how to put in photos, links, various file types, I’m happy with the simple rich text navigation. I’ve tried too many apps with no rich text, that seem impossible to put new files into notebooks, don’t have different levels of bolding, won’t allow strike-through… but… BUT! I can make a card! WTF‽ 

The majority of Notes remain on my devices although I have 2 Tb of Cloud storage. Maybe I thought the Cloud would abhor a vacuum and pull my Notes over. Nope. I’ve taken to copying files - Notes within Folders- to other apps when I try them so I have bits of things everywhere. I don’t think I’m going to lose my data but I can’t do much with it now and I don’t even have a better place to store new information until I figure out something new.

title: Apple pencil thickness options are ridiculous after software upgrade
body: With the recent software upgrade the thickness options for the pencil tool in Notes are ridiculous. Previously you could select the thickness of the pencil tool in the Notes app from five thickness options. To use an analogy, if the thinnest pencil setting was 10 mph, the next thickness option would be 20 mph, the next 30 mph, with the thickest option being 50 mph. This gave a reasonable range of thicknesses to choose from and more importantly, each step up was reasonable, so it went from thin, to a bit thicker, to a medium size, to a thick pencil, etc. Something like the equivalent of a fine pencil, to HB, to 2B, 4B, 6B, etc., in a real pencil. After the recent software upgrade the options start at 5mph, the next setting is 50 mph, 70 mph, etc. None of the options are really workable. The thinnest pencil option is too thin and the next thinnest is far too thick. The thicker options are just ridiculous — who would ever use these? To put it in terms of an actual pencil, the options as they are now are ‘extra fine’, 4B, 8B, etc. — there is nothing in the middle range. Contrast this with what it was previously, i.e. fine pencil, to HB, to 2B, 4B, 6B, etc. Turning the Apple Pencil at an angle has always allowed you to make much thicker lines and shading, so I don’t get the point of the these very thick settings. I can only suggest that these various settings have been chosen by a developer who doesn’t actually use an Apple Pencil in the Notes app. Please change the range of settings available for the pencil tool, by narrowing the range of thicknesses options available and adding more middle options with smaller step ups between each option. At the moment it’s unusable (at least for this user). What you need, to match a real pencil, is ‘fine’, HB, 2B, 4B, 6B, not 24B. I note that the highlighter tool suffers from the same problem. It is really annoying when software upgrades take a great product and &%£@ it up.

title: Typical Apple Mediocrity
body:
Apple is a great company. iPads and iPhones are 2nd to none. So why is it that every single native app is always—without exception—the most mediocre and limited offering imaginable? Alarm clock app? Unreliable and barely works. Podcast app? Unusable by any measure. Calendar app? Welcome to 2007 technology! And here, the Notes app: a product that is so minimalist that it barely—barely—rates above sticking a “post it” on the screen of your phone

Apple Notes lacks so many features of 3rd party apps, it’s hard to know where to start. The pen selection is the worst I’ve ever seen; I can’t find a single one that feels comfortable or satisfying to write with. The lack of any sort of useable interaction between text and Apple Pencil is mind boggling (ex: To Do lists with checkboxes). Note covers? Nah. Layers? Don’t even ask. Multi-image import? Forget about it. Record lecture notes? Please; that kind of fancy footwork is for city slickers. 

I guess that Apple is perfectly content to make world class hardware and embarrassing applications. You’d think that at some point, pride would set in and they’d try to do better, but no. Notes, Podcasts, Photos, Calendar, and Clock have all been an embarrassment for as long as I can remember; their only idea of innovation was to remove the lowercase “i” from the name of each app (and even that was a mistake that was pointless and just flat-out dumb, unless they wanted to purposely distance themselves from their own incredibly bland app offerings). Notes has been limited, boring, and bad ever since it made its debut, and barring an Apple recommitment to being the best at everything they do, I don’t see that changing anytime soon.

title: iCloud Notes (web-based) no search function within a note
body:
The mobile app has a Find in Note feature but you have to tap once, scroll down before tapping again.  It would be more convenient if there’s already a search bar within a note 

iCloud Notes, when used on a browser (PC), is quite annoying in that it had absolutely no search function WITHIN A NOTE. Sure, you can do a search among notes and it will show all the notes that presumably have that word. However, when u open the note, it doesn’t bring you immediately to that searched word and there’s no way to find all the occurrences of that search word. 

Ctrl-F doesn’t work within a note. It would be really convenient if Apple would make it possible for Ctrl-F to be functional. 

Also, the usual navigating keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl left and right arrows, Ctrl-Shft arrows) don’t work within a note. 

The only good thing about iCloud Notes is that it syncs across all my Apple devices.

title: Lovely for writing stories, lists, bucketlists, etc!
body:
I use this app for ALL my writing, and I capitalize all for a reason. Since I first got my phone, I have been searching for a app that is private and that I can share my note with somebody. This is the exact app I was looking for. Firstly, when you start your note, it lets you TITLE it, unlike some apps that just make a note and you have to remember the paragraph. Second, it lets you use copy and paste fonts. I have had SO, SO, so many apps that you put different fonts that you copy and pasted in, come out as ugly boxed x’s. This app is different, and perfect. It also gives you unlimited access, unlike most other apps that cost money to write one thing down. Thank you Apple, for making that. I also like how when you put a • and write something, (like a bucket-list), and you press return, it types it for you! This lets my hands take a break from having to go the the 123 keyboard, to the #+= keyboard and press •. It also lets you share it with people in your messages, and through other websites. I love this part, specifically because it gives you the option for you to let them edit it, or view it. Once, I didn’t know that was a option so one of my friends thought it would be funny to mess around with my work. I ended up re-fixing it and finding out you could let people view it only. Thank you for that. 

- a pleased downloader and girl who’s hoping to be an author, thanks to this app: (and who’s hands are hurting from writing so much)

title: The bones are there, but it needs work
body:
Apple is SO close on Notes. It is easy to use, searches inside documents, handles handwriting (and makes it searchable) syncs quickly and in my experience reliably.

But the note-taking experience itself…meh. Limited options for formatting, no versioning, can’t even resize an image or use colors

Thing is, Apple has an excellent editor in Pages, and they obviously understand versioning (all of their productivity apps do it). They could bring that stuff into Notes and quickly elevate it.

The full wishlist would be
* Web clipper (really, there should be an iOS/macOS level web clipper)
* Markdown support for writing & exporting
* Nested tags
* File provider - e.g. the ability to edit a file attached to a Note and have it save back to the Note, rather than needing to delete and re-attach every time.

In the meantime, it’s fine to use for quick note capture, but there are better tools available for serious note taking/second brain usage.

title: The best app on the iPhone
body:
Apple's minimalist philosophy is great, but when it comes to actually implementing minimalism it is always a hit or miss. Sometimes they screw up, like with Music, but sometimes they create a masterpiece, like Notes. Notes does everything I want it to every time. I have never wanted to go searching for another app to replace it. I have never needed to. It seems like a simple little app at first, but there's so much beneath the hood, that is brilliantly hidden from the user. It is not just minimalism done right, it is minimalism done PERFECT. 
There is no better note taking app. Every other one has some annoying interface full of pop ups, pestering me to sign into this or upgrade to this or check out this feature, it makes me want to pull my hair out. Meanwhile Notes lets me do what I came there to do: write. It is the perfect app for the crafting text. It is fast and to the point, simple yet has everything I could ever want.
In conclusion, I love Notes.

title: Recent Font Issue
body: I’ve used this app for years to keep track of my to do lists etc. it’s always been great, and I’ve never had an issue until recently. However, in the past few months I’ve experienced a strange bug that is really ruining my experience. For some reason, the issue only occurs when I have a line of text that’s double spaced (I hit “return” twice before it) to create an empty line above it, which separates it from the text above. If I place the cursor to the left of the text and hit “delete” to delete the return and remove the empty line above it, the font for the text on that line changes to a smaller, uglier font that is hard to read. It only changes for the line immediately after the deleted return. All of the lines below it remain in the standard notes font. This is super annoying, because it happens every time and there’s not even a way to change the font in notes. It’s such a stupid bug I would have expected it to have been fixed months ago. I’m not sure why it would even occur in the first place. Please fix this! I’ll change my review to 5 stars as soon as it’s fixed. iPhone X with latest software updates.

title: After 1,000 notes later…
body:
Let’s just start with the fact that I have over 1,000 notes saved in the app!!! Probably not what the “typical” user would have, but I found that it works for me. Here’s the HOW and WHY I use this Notes App. 

It’s a simple tool that I use to store and organize info that I come back to on a regular basis. It’s hard enough to remember “everything” that happens in a day, let alone that IDEA I thought of yesterday or info SNIPPET I found last week and WHERE I found it or bookmarked it. 

For example: I have a main folder for “Gardening”, with related notes to reference. I “pin” the ones I view constantly. Then there’s sub-folders for Ailments, Fertilizers, Methods, Soil, and Schedules. Each folder contains specific notes and photos on that topic. 

Some of my other main folders include: Accounts, Automotive, Health, Home Repairs, Leatherwork, Woodworking, and Work Related. 

After trying other apps and methods to organize the same way, the Notes App just seems to be the simplest way to do what I need. (Since it’s from Apple, it will always be available and automatically syncs between my phone and computer, which is a huge reason I use it this way). 

I have also utilized almost every app feature, from web links to #tags, pinned notes (for hierarchy) to folders and sub-folders (for list organization), and even formatting the notes with Headers, indents, photos, columns and bullet types. Other apps have more features, but most things you’d need can be done within the current Notes features. 

A cool “search” feature, is that the app can return “text” results found within a photo. 

While there is a lot you can do with the app, there are still a few limitations, glitches and areas for improvement. Apple constantly fixes and improves the app, so I just confidently wait for each update. 

One feature I would LOVE to see added, is the ability to create a link to other notes within my notes library. #Tags sort of does it, but not as well as a SIMPLE LINK to a note file. That’s my wish. 

I hope this review helps other users.

title: Forgotten Passcode for locked notes
body:
The Notes app allows users to lock and secure their notes with a passcode. Once you forget that passcode, there is no way of unlocking those locked (now lost forever) important notes.

The Face ID feature would be the only feature that would help prevent being locked out of your locked notes forever but the Face ID feature stops popping up. The Notes app then only requests for the passcode (which in this and many other people's cases are forgotten).You can reset your passcode but it only affects the new notes , not your old locked notes.

Apple should work on fixing this issue because it’s affecting many people and keeping us out of our important notes. Apple should put a “Forgot Passcode” option , where users can verify themselves and never get locked out of their notes. Apple should also keep the Face ID feature enabled at all times , so it can help us get over the forgotten passcode. 

This is an issue that I and many others are currently having. It's frustrating and makes users feel hopeless about their locked notes. This is something that I wouldn't expect from a great company like Apple. I have seen many Apple forums and spoke to Apple customer support myself, there is no way to help people unlock their locked notes.

Thank you and I hope that this will be fixed soon in a future update.

title: Fast, quick notes! Some feature requests
body:
Love how fast and straightforward it is to take notes. You can even tell Siri to “note that….” and it will create a note for you. Love folders and the ability to insert pictures and drawings. This means that there is very little delay from the moment you think of the note to the moment you write it. 

The new Smart Folders feature is pretty cool, but I would like to request that it please be enhanced to allow “sub folders” to be Smart Folders. 

Currently, all Smart Folders must be at the main folder level. This can cause things to be very cluttered and doesn’t help with organization.

For example, I have a folder called “ideas.” I’d love to use tags to automatically sort those notes into a variety of sub folders. However, if I create a smart folder, it is forced to be a main level folder, and cannot be a subfolder within the “ideas” folder.”

This means that all my Smart Folders related to “ideas” will appear at the top level hierarchy along with my other folders such as Recipes, Trip Planning, and Fitness, which are not related to my “ideas” folder.

This causes a lot of clutter.

title: Error known to Apple since 2021 in iOS prevents this app from working correctly
body:
I took my iPhone SE 2nd generation into the Apple Store at Hilldale Mall in Madison, Wisconsin on Wednesday, November 17, and again on Monday, November 22, 2021 for the Notes app crashing unexpectedly. I have purchased a new iPhone 13 in April 2022, and the same issue affects iOS 15.4.1.

The Apple Notes app in MacOS for Monterey, in iPadOS 15, and in the web-based version on iCloud.com all perform as expected.

Apple elevated my case to service “Level 2” in the fall and connected me by phone with an engineer.

After extensive troubleshooting, including forced app closure, disabling synchronization and then toggling it on again, deleting the iOS Notes app and reinstalling it, and then erasing the phone and reinstalling apps from scratch (not restoring from backup), the issue persisted. It continues on my new IPhone 13.

Apple’s engineer indicated this is a known problem with iOS Notes in fall, but there is not timeline for a software patch.

I have 3,094 notes approaching a few gigabytes in size — making me a power user by most accounts.

Be VERY wary of using this app for since it does not work on iOS devices if used extensively!!!

body:
Far too much built-in unhelpful helpfulness.

Stuff you CANNOT stop from happening. Just like those auto-down window buttons that insist on going all the way UP, or all the way DOWN, over and over, and you just want it cracked open an inch. Except NOT like that, because you can eventually get that window almost right. 

I want CONTROL.

But Apple knows better. Apple wants to do it FOR you. Because Apple is mommy. Because You baby. And Mommy knows. Mommy always knows.

Apple will to do FOR you what YOU wanted to do, so that you don't have to.

And Mommy Apple WILL do it. To keep your life simple.

Trying to edit a paragraph that has URLs in it? You're in an editor, but Apple thinks you might really prefer a browser. So links are linkable, like in a browser, but they aren't editable, like in an editor. They do everything BUT edit. Even if you OPENED THE NOTES APP EXPRESSLY FOR THE PURPOSE OF EDITING URLS.

Trying to fix weird stuff that happened during a cut/paste? Good luck. Some text pasted as really small font in your email app, so you brought it HERE to fix the fontsize weirdness and repaste it back into a fresh email? Good luck. Weird fontsize discrepancies will only get WORSE here. You're not in an actual text editor. It's more of a Ouija board. Actual text output is under the control of unseen spirits, AI mindreading modules, and bad software design choices.

Files that you can't find, file modifications that you can't undo, text editing behaviours that are sometimes useful, but which you cannot override. Bizarre Cut/Paste errors that indicate the presence of very sloppy text-handling code underneath. title: Deletions
body: The problem with this app is that it is designed in a way that makes it almost inevitable that you will delete information. Recently while editing a note, I realized that I had recorded some data in the wrong note. I highlight the text so that I could cut or delete it but that option was not available. Among others I had the option of copying it but no simple delete was offered. So I had to manually starting from the end of the sentence hold down the backspace until the data was removed totally. But that is because it takes too long to hit it repeatedly and it proceeds much more quickly to hold it down. So it starts with one letter at a time and does this for several letters, then will delete words one at a time, but then very quickly if you continue holding it down it will delete your entire note. This all takes place within a span of a couple or three seconds. There is no time to react to it. Once the note is gone, there is no means to recover. I am told shaking the phone will undo your most recent action. But why not just place an option on the screen to undo? There is no security to protect the notes using save in which case changes could be discarded if you are not satisfied with them, or can continue in a state of edit. In short, not a single thing which could be done to protect your data is done to protect it. This app is among the very worst.

As if I cared about their opinions! Otherwise, it is a vary bare-bones app taking experience . Simple and effective and clean-looking. Hashtags are new, and they make sorting individual notes better, but absolutely none of this is worth trading in for the absolutely criminal lack of metric data! You won’t know who is reading or how many or from where. No room for comments or likes or anything. You’re very lives are in the hands of just about everyone. What they collectively decide to do with you is anyone’s guess.

body:
The notes app has been a love hate relationship as an iPhone user. The sheer amount of words that it holds is incredible. Though with that comes lagging. Over the course of the past month I've used this app for larger note taking such as random ideas to safe keep, places to go, bucket lists, etc. Yet even though it has a low amount of words the typing slows down and lags behind significantly. It also freezes when a collaborator edits, leaving you with a stuck drop menu that's at the bottom and who edited it at the top. I hope these things can be fixed, whether adding a higher word limit to slow lag or to look into the new update for bugs.

title: Promising but buggy
body:
I wish I can give this app 5 stars, because I love using it with the Apple Pencil. 
However, it is very difficult to see an app riddles with so bugs coming from the biggest company in the world, and bugs that have been around for years:
- switching away from the app and back resets the ink, eraser and highlighter settings, without reflecting that in the UI. I have to change them back and forth every time I return to the app
- switching back and forth also often selects the first pinned note instead of the last edited note. And I have to reopen the side panel, scroll through notes, and select the one I was working on
- if you chose not to hide the floating UI, the app will still hide it after you start writing, and you have to reopen that UI again every time you need to switch tools.  And in the latest version, it moves by itself from top to bottom and you need to bring it back up again. 
On top of that, the floating UI violates a UX heuristic: it blocks the UI underneath it and part of the notes. Why not just integrate it with the top toolbar? There is plenty of space. 

I like the ink in this app more than any other app, but I’m gradually switching to OneNote due to its robustness and reliability.

title: Too slow! Cannot retrieve old locked notes if forgot password!
body:
Usually don't rate apps, but this definitely needs to be addressed. There is no way to contact anyone of problems for this app.

Notes has been very slow and sluggish for many years. People are complaining about this, but there is no solution.  They have not fixed this problem with updates. Why?  It has been very frustrating working with this app when typing in app is very glitchy and very slow to type.  

Not only this, but recently if you forgot your password for your locked old notes, then you no longer can retrieve old notes by changing one password.  If you change password, then this new password applies to new notes, not old. 

It used to be one password that can unlock all notes, but now it has been changed. When and why?  What is the point of locking notes if you cannot change password if you forgot password of old notes???

Having visible "undo" function would be better instead of shaking phone which does not work all of the time.

Will change rating if the above recurring problem is fixed. In the meantime, need to find another notes app that is more reliable.

title: Errors for over a year
body:
For over a year the app has been having interface (?) errors that have lead to lost work and annoyances.

Loading the app, it may load into a prior note, but there’s no text in the body of the note. You then have to clear the app and re-open. This has happened since I got my 12 in December 2020. Daily. You’d think it would have been fixed in the updates since then but it continues to occur. 

Or, the app will erase an entire note while you’re working on it and it returns to the main list of your existing apps, wiping out the work in progress and making it impossible to ‘undo’ or something to that extent. This has happened ~3-5 times on my 12.

Not all is bad, they’ve added some cool new features making the app more interactive but I can’t help wonder if these contribute to these interface issues. Please fix these though, I just lost an hours worth of notes for homework 🥺

title: Not good for students taking handwritten notes
body:
If you are a student, do NOT use this app for taking notes. There are two key reasons why this app is horrible for important notes: (1) use of raster ink instead of vector-based graphics and (2) extremely poor options for exporting/sharing notes.

(1) When you are taking handwritten notes in Apple Notes, the pen strokes are rasterized, not vector-based. As a consequence, you cannot zoom into your notes without experiencing a decrease in visual resolution. Thankfully, this is not such a big issue when reading notes in the app on your iPad because the resolution is high enough that everything remains perfectly legible. However, the rasterized pen strokes lead us to our second problem: low resolution when exporting/sharing notes.

(2) Imagine that you’ve diligently taken several lectures worth of notes for your class, and would like to view these notes on your laptop or desktop computer. Thankfully, Apple Notes saves your handwritten notes to iCloud, so you should be able to properly view your notes on your computer, right? WRONG. While the notes saved locally on your iPad in Apple Notes are viewable in full resolution, the notes in iCloud are saved in a much lower resolution, to the point where they are nearly illegible. Oh well, maybe instead you can export your notes from your iPad as a pdf and view it that way? NOPE. The same issue occurs: for some reason, Apple Notes has a file size cap on exported pdfs, so your beautiful notes will be unreadable after your export them. Oh, your classmate wants you to share your notes with them? Surely sharing the notes via iCloud or email would do the trick? HAHA OF COURSE NOT. The exported file will be in low resolution due to the file size cap. 

For the love of all that is good, DO NOT USE THIS APP.
